question.prompt: In year \(N,\) the \(300\)th day of the year is a Tuesday. In year \(N + 1,\) the \(200\)th day is also a Tuesday. On what day of the week did the \(100\)th day of year \(N - 1\) occur?

solutions.explanation:
Two dates fall on the same weekday exactly when the number of days between them is a multiple of \(7\). Let \(L\) be the number of days in year \(N\). From its \(300\)th day to the \(200\)th day of year \(N+1\), the elapsed time is
\[
(L-300)+200=L-100.
\]
A year has \(365\) or \(366\) days, so this difference is \(265\) or \(266\). Since
\[
265=37\cdot7+6,
\qquad 266=38\cdot7,
\]
the two Tuesdays force \(L=366\). Thus year \(N\) is a leap year, and its preceding year \(N-1\) has \(365\) days because consecutive years cannot both be leap years.

From the \(100\)th day of year \(N-1\) to the \(300\)th day of year \(N\), the elapsed time is
\[
(365-100)+300=565=80\cdot7+5
\]
days. Therefore Tuesday is five weekdays after the requested day. Five days before Tuesday is \(\boxed{\text{Thursday}}\), choice A.
solutions.title: Count elapsed days in whole weeks
